First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int {e}^{px+q}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{p}{e}^{px+q}+C
$$

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{2}{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}\frac{3}{2}{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-\frac{1}{5}{e}^{-5x}]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(-\frac{1}{5}{e}^{-5a}+\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{5}{lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{-5a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={e}^{-5x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{e}^{-5x}=\infty $

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{e}^{-5x}=0$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14047719/assets/5010180e9cd41608abc630cd8974cc69ee78337bcb46a7f079d58eeb8dda9cc2.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{2}{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{5}{lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{-5a}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\frac{1}{5}-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
